answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the gale schedule in the beacon ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the grove checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 4 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 94 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden legitimate agents do not face at scale. That is 14 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
